**Finding submitted: needs_review (LICENSE), no redline proposed.**

Summary of the review:

- **Document type mismatch.** This is a Verizon ABS transfer and servicing agreement. Full-text searches for grant language ("grants to", "non-exclusive", "right to use", software/systems access, IP/trademark) returned no licence grant of any kind running to the Issuer or Depositor.
- **All "licence" hits are non-responsive.** p0234, p0259 and p0272 are regulatory due-qualification representations ("necessary licenses and approvals"), not grants.
- **The only licence-adjacent provision is a disclaimer.** Section 7.4 (p0346) states the Servicer "will not be obligated to provide, license or assign its processes, procedures, models, servicing software or other applications to any Successor Servicer or any third party." That is a transition/IP allocation term, assessed under IP/TRANSITION, and I did not double-flag it here.
- **Why not "missing" with an insertion.** Both fallback elements presuppose an existing licence — affiliate coverage on written notice and transfer to an M&A successor. With no licensed subject matter under this contract, the shortest conforming clause would still be a fabricated software licence grant, which exceeds the checklist ceiling and would insert a bargain the parties never struck. The successor provisions at p0249 and p0348 concern assumption of the Agreement itself, not licensed rights.
- **Escalation point for the deal team:** if the Issuer or a Successor Servicer is commercially expected to obtain rights in Cellco's servicing platform, that should be negotiated into the Section 7.4 transition provision rather than added as a generic licence grant.
